name: weatherlog
description: Weather station readings: unit conversion, range validation, daily aggregates, alert rules and CSV export.
author: test2 author (independent of the reviewer)

issues.description: The limits are documented as inclusive but the upper bound is excluded, so 100% humidity, 500 mm of rain or 60 C are refused.
issues.fix_hint: Compare the upper bound with <= as well.

issues.description: A reading back within the limit should end the station's run, but the run counter is left as it is, so non-consecutive breaches add up and fire the rule.
issues.fix_hint: Reset the station's run to 0 when the value is within the limit.

issues.description: The default rejected list is created once and shared by every Ingestor built without one, so rejections leak between ingestors.
issues.fix_hint: Default to None and create a new list per instance.

issues.description: The station id (which comes from station payloads) is used as a file name without checks, so an id like '../x' writes outside the export folder.
issues.fix_hint: Reject station ids that are not a plain file name, or check the resolved path stays inside the folder.

issues.description: aggregate imports alerts only for FROST_LIMIT_C while alerts imports aggregate for daily summaries, making the two modules circular.

issues.anchor: def ingest_batch(self, batch: dict[str, Any], now: datetime | None = None) -> int:
issues.description: Six levels of nested if/for; guard clauses and a helper per item would flatten it.
The m/s to km/h factor 3.6 is repeated in three modules instead of living in units.py next to the other conversions.

decoys.why_it_is_fine: It iterates over a copy of the keys, so deleting from the dict inside the loop is safe.
MD5 is only a change-detection checksum for exported files, not a security control, and is marked usedforsecurity=False.
